units.source_text: “我还是书生的时候，看到过一个贤女之流的人。

en.t: When I was still a student, I once knew a woman who was the very model of a wise lady.

units.source_text: 这个人就像刚才左马头讲的那人一样，国家大事也谈得来，私人生活、处世之道方面也有高明见解。

en.t: Like the woman the Captain of the Left Horse Guard just described, she could discuss affairs of state and also had excellent judgment about private life and the ways of the world.

units.source_text: 讲到才学，直教半通不通的博士惭愧无地。

en.t: As for learning and talent, she could make a half-educated scholar feel so ashamed he would have nowhere to hide.

units.source_text: 不拘谈论何事，总使得对方不得开口。

en.t: Whatever the subject of discussion, she always left the other person unable to get a word in.

units.source_text: 我怎么认识她的呢？

en.t: How did I come to know her?

units.source_text: 那时我到一位文章博士[\[17\]](#part1331.html#m17)家里去，请他教授汉诗汉文。

en.t: At that time I used to visit the home of a Doctor of Letters[\[17\]](#part1331.html#m17), asking him to teach me Chinese poetry and prose.

units.source_text: 听说这位博士有好几个女儿，我便找个机会，向一个女儿求爱。

en.t: Hearing that this scholar had several daughters, I found an opportunity and began courting one of them.

units.source_text: 父母知道了，办起酒来，举杯庆祝，那位文章博士就即座高吟‘听我歌两途’[\[18\]](#part1331.html#m18)。

en.t: When her parents learned of it, they prepared wine and raised their cups in celebration, and the Doctor of Letters at once chanted aloud, 'Listen as I sing of the two paths'[\[18\]](#part1331.html#m18).

units.source_text: 我同这个女子其实感情并不十分融洽，只因不宜辜负父母好意，也就和她厮混下去。

en.t: In truth, my feelings with this woman were not especially harmonious, but since it would not do to disappoint her parents' kindness, I continued keeping company with her.

units.source_text: 这期间，这女子对我照料得非常周到：枕上私语，也都是关于我身求学之事，以及将来为官作宰的知识。

en.t: During that time, she looked after me with extraordinary care: even our pillow talk was all about my studies and the knowledge I would need someday to hold office and govern.

units.source_text: 凡人生大事，她都教我。

en.t: She taught me everything important in life.

units.source_text: 她的书牍也写得极好：一个假名[\[19\]](#part1331.html#m19)也不用，全用汉字，措辞冠冕堂皇，潇洒不俗。

en.t: Her letters were also beautifully written: she did not use a single kana[\[19\]](#part1331.html#m19), writing entirely in Chinese characters, with language that was dignified, elegant, and never vulgar.

units.source_text: 这样，我自然和她亲近起来，把她当作老师，学得了一些歪诗拙文。

en.t: In this way I naturally grew close to her, treated her as my teacher, and learned from her a little of my clumsy poetry and awkward prose.

units.source_text: 我到现在也不忘记她的师恩。

en.t: Even now I have not forgotten the debt I owe her as my teacher.

units.source_text: 可是，我不能把她看作一个恩爱而可靠的妻子，因为像我这样不学无术的人，万一有时举止不端，在她面前现丑，是很可耻的。

en.t: And yet I could not regard her as an affectionate and dependable wife, because for an ignorant, unlearned man like me, it would be terribly shameful if I ever behaved improperly and made a fool of myself before her.

units.source_text: 像你们那样的贵公子，更用不着此种机巧泼辣的内助。

en.t: Gentlemen of rank like you have even less need for such a clever and forceful helpmate.

units.source_text: 我明知此种人不宜为妻，然而为了宿世因缘，也就迁就了。

en.t: I knew perfectly well that such a person was not suited to be a wife, but because of karmic ties from a former life, I gave in and accommodated myself to her.

units.source_text: 总之，男子实在是无聊的啊！”

en.t: In short, men really are worthless creatures!"

units.source_text: 说到这里，暂时住口。

en.t: Having said this much, he fell silent for a while.

units.source_text: 头中将要他快讲下去，催促着说：“啊，这倒真是一个很有意思的女子！”

en.t: The Secretary Captain urged him to continue quickly, saying, "Ah, now she really does sound like a fascinating woman!"

units.source_text: 式部丞明知这是捧场，仍然得意扬扬地讲下去：

en.t: The Assistant Secretary of the Ministry of Ceremonial knew perfectly well this was mere encouragement, but he still went on speaking with great satisfaction:
